text.p: Food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday it was comfortable with analysts' forecasts for a net profit of about A$115 million for the full year to June 30, 1997. Goodman also said it was looking for Australasian acquisitions.

Goodman chief executive David Hearn repeated his previous forecast of double digit earnings growth for the full fiscal year and noted that analysts forecasts of full year pre-abnormals net profit were centred around A$115 million.
"That's not a number we are uncomfortable with," Hearn told a media briefing.
Hearn said Goodman Fielder's priority was to build a world-class food group and expand into areas where it could use its competitive strength.
Money raised by the A$300 million sale of the Meneba NV milling and baking business in Europe would initially be used to repay debt.
The group's gearing would fall from around 48 percent to about 20 percent, he said. Further out, the funds would be used for either internal investment or acquisitions.
"The emphasis will be on New Zealand and Australia," Hearn said.
